answer: Each identity must grow one juniper in a shared grove: a sequential memory-hard proof chained to that identity's own non-transferable tenure, computed step by step and impossible to parallelise or hand to a clone. A fable of one farmer planting many saplings fails here, because each juniper demands its own full sequential computation and its own tenure history — splitting tenure across n clones restarts every proof from zero, so the attacker's cost grows with every head while one honest identity keeps a single compounding proof.
